'''Helen Vaughn Michel''' (born 1932) is an American chemist best known for her efforts in fields including [[analytical chemistry]] and [[archaeological science]], and specific processes such as [[neutron activation analysis]] and [[radiocarbon dating]]. Her work with [[Frank Asaro]] at the [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]] at the [[University of California, Berkeley|University of California (Berkeley)]] is particularly noteworthy as it includes the dating of [[Drake's Plate of Brass]] as well as the [[Alvarez hypothesis]], the hypothesis that posits the [[Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event]].<ref name="wayne">{{cite book|last=Wayne|first=Tiffany|title=American Women of Science Since 1900 / Vol. 1, Essays, A-H.|year=2011|publisher=[[ABC-CLIO]]|isbn=978-1598841589|pages=688&ndash;689}}</ref>

Michel retired from the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory in 1990.<ref name="wayne"/>
